newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS KEEP A WARY EYE ON AJAX'S LITMANEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS KEEP A WARY EYE ON AJAX'S LITMANEN.

text.p: Jari Litmanen will get special treatment from a wary Juventus on Wednesday when the holders meet Ajax in a European Cup semifinal second leg rerun of last year's final.

The Dutch team's tricky Finn has turned into something of an obsession for Juventus after scoring against the Italians in their two previous European Cup encounters in the past 12 months, including the 1996 final in Rome.
Juventus and Italy defender Ciro Ferrara made no bones about who he and his team mates considered the main danger standing between them and a second consecutive final.

"(Goalkeeper Angelo) Peruzzi has already started to warn us," Ferrara said before the Amsterdam side arrived in Italy in search of their third consecutive final appearance. "He keeps on telling us to keep an eye on him."

"I think he is pretty much outstanding. He's hard to control, he moves around a lot and finds the openings. He scored in Amsterdam because he found the space while in Rome he took advantage of one of our defensive errors," Ferrara said.
Litmanen, the only Ajax player asked for autographs when the team arrived at Turin airport on Tuesday, is reportedly recovering from an injury.
"I'll have a final fitness test at the Delle Alpi tomorrow. I really hope to make it," Litmanen said.

Few in Italy took those words with anything other than a pinch of salt, detecting instead some last-minute behind-the-scenes gamesmanship by crafty coach Louis Van Gaal. Something that Litmanen himself seemed to betray.
"Even if I'm not at my best, I'll be there," he said. "I cannot miss one of the most important matches of my career. I'll talk to the doctors, we'll find a solution."
The Italians won 2-1 in Amsterdam earlier in the month, meaning Ajax must score two in Turin to progress, after winning the cup on penalties last year.

The task is by no means impossible for Ajax since Juventus beat Borussia Dortmund 3-1 away in 1995 and then lost 2-1 at the Delle Alpi in November that year. They are unbeaten at home in the European Cup since that date.

While Litmanen is sure to be on the pitch, Juventus once again must do without Alessandro Del Piero who has not recovered from a muscle injury. They also have Yugoslav midfielder Vladimir Jugovic suspended for one match.
Just as worrying for Juve, they also have nine players facing suspension from the final if they pick up another booking -- a factor that could lead to a dose of caution.

Croat Alen Boksic, who scored his first league goal in 129 days with the winner against Bologna on Saturday to send Juve six points clear in the league, will be the main target man up front alongside young Italy international Christian Vieri.
Alessio Tacchinardi, 21, replaces Jugovic.
Ajax are missing Dutch international Patrick Kluivert, who underwent surgery on his knee two weeks ago and appears to have played his last game for the club before joining AC Milan.
Key defender Winston Bogarde, who scored twice against NEC Nijmegen on Friday, appears to have overcome an ankle injury while winger Tijani Babangida has a slight knee problem.
The statistics prove only that both teams are hard to beat.

Ajax have not lost an away match in the European Cup since the Champions League started in 1992 and have a habit of playing better away than at home, while Juventus have not been beaten by the Dutch team in Italy in three matches since 1975.
Probable teams:
Juventus - Angelo Peruzzi; Sergio Porrini, Mark Iuliano, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Montero, Angelo Di Livio, Alessio Tacchinardi, Zinedine Zidane, Didier Deschamps, Christian Vieri, Alen Boksic.
Ajax - Edwin van der Sar; Mario Melchiot, Danny Blind, Frank de Boer, Winston Bogarde; Jari Litmanen, Arnold Scholten, Richard Witschge, Tijani Babangida, Marc Overmars, Ronald de Boer.
